_schema.subject: server/watch/diarize.py speech_segments (energy VAD + merge-gap + min-duration)
_schema.description: Golden test vectors for the energy VAD that turns raw PCM into (start_s, end_s) speech spans. Each case describes a synthetic int16 mono signal as a sequence of constant-loudness stretches; the consumer generates the PCM deterministically from that spec (see `signal`), runs its VAD with `config`, and asserts the returned spans equal `expected` within `tolerance_s`. Timestamps in seconds as floats. Language-neutral on purpose so a Kotlin/TypeScript port of the VAD can consume the same file.

signal.generator: Concatenate the stretches in order. Each stretch is `seconds` long (sample count = floor(seconds * sample_rate)). A stretch with `dbfs: null` is digital silence (all zeros). Otherwise it is a pure sine at `tone_hz` (case-level, default 150.0), phase starting at 0 for EVERY stretch, whose RMS is `dbfs` dB relative to int16 full scale (32768): amplitude = 32768 * 10^(dbfs/20) * sqrt(2), cast to int16. The RMS of a sine is amplitude/sqrt(2), so this lands the stretch on the requested dBFS (to within the sub-cycle truncation error of a stretch that isn't a whole number of periods — negligible at these margins).
signal.dbfs: float or null — RMS loudness of the stretch in dBFS. The VAD's `floor_dbfs` is compared with strict `>` (a frame AT the floor is silence), so cases stay well clear of the floor on both sides unless they are specifically probing it

config.floor_dbfs: float — frames with RMS at/under this are silence (default -45.0, shared with the streaming VectorEngine so 'speech' means one thing)
config.frame_seconds: float — VAD frame length (default 0.25); a trailing sub-frame shorter than this is still evaluated, not dropped
config.merge_gap_seconds: float — adjacent speech runs separated by a gap <= this (inclusive) are one turn (default 0.30)
config.min_seconds: float — merged spans shorter than this (strict <) are dropped as coughs/clicks (default 0.60). Merging happens BEFORE this filter, so two sub-minimum bursts across a short gap survive as one turn

_schema.expected: list of {start_s, end_s} spans, in time order
_schema.tolerance_s: float — absolute tolerance on each boundary. Spans are frame-aligned in the reference implementation, so this only needs to absorb float accumulation of frame boundaries, not detection jitter

cases.name: silence_only
cases.description: Pure digital silence yields no spans at all (rms is -inf, never above the floor). Source: test_speech_segments_pure_silence_is_empty.

cases.name: one_burst
cases.description: A single 2 s burst is one span covering exactly its frames.

cases.name: two_bursts_merged_across_short_gap
cases.description: A one-frame (0.25 s <= 0.30 s merge gap) pause does not split a turn: two 1 s bursts become one 2.25 s span. Source: test_speech_segments_merges_a_short_gap.

cases.name: two_bursts_kept_apart_across_long_gap
cases.description: A 1 s pause (> merge gap) keeps two 2 s bursts as separate turns. Source: test_speech_segments_finds_two_bursts.

cases.name: two_frame_gap_splits
cases.description: Merge-gap boundary from the other side: a two-frame (0.5 s > 0.30 s) pause is a real turn boundary even though each burst is only 1 s.

cases.name: burst_too_short_dropped
cases.description: A single-frame (0.25 s < 0.60 s) blip is a cough, not a turn: only the 2 s burst survives, starting after the blip and its 1 s gap. Source: test_speech_segments_drops_too_short_bursts.

cases.name: merge_happens_before_min_duration_drop
cases.description: Ordering of the two clean-up passes: two 0.5 s bursts (each alone < 0.60 s) across a one-frame gap merge into a 1.25 s span FIRST, so neither is dropped.

cases.name: mixed_conversation_shape
cases.description: Everything at once: leading silence, a turn with an internal one-frame pause (merged), a long gap, a one-frame cough (dropped), another long gap, a final turn, trailing silence.

cases.name: quiet_tone_under_floor_is_silence
cases.description: Loudness, not just non-zero samples, decides speech: a 2 s tone at -50 dBFS (under the -45 floor) is silence.

cases.name: tone_just_over_floor_is_speech
cases.description: The floor is a threshold, not a comfort margin: -40 dBFS (5 dB over the floor) is speech.

cases.name: trailing_sub_frame_is_evaluated
cases.description: A clip whose length isn't a frame multiple: the last 0.125 s partial frame is still scored, so the span runs to the true end (1.125 s), not the last full frame (1.0 s). Source: test_speech_segments_includes_trailing_sub_frame_speech.
